thread:
mira: Heads up — found a nasty edge in the Kotlin SDK sample app on Android 14. When sending a streaming POST (RequestBody with writeTo streaming), if the server returns a 401 and our client retries, the body is sometimes sent twice (duplicate records). Repro on Pixel 8 emulator.
dan: streaming POST? you mean Transfer-Encoding: chunked and not buffered first?
mira: exactly. our sample uploader writes a streaming RequestBody that isn't repeatable. OkHttp retries on some connection failures (or when Authenticator triggers) and re-sends the call, which leads to the server seeing duplicate payloads. logs show two identical payloads within 200ms.
li: can you paste the simplified RequestBody code?
mira: sure — trimmed down:
```kotlin
class StreamingBody(private val source: InputStream): RequestBody() {
  override fun contentType() = "application/octet-stream".toMediaType()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) {
    source.source().use { it.readAll(sink) }
  }
}
```
mia: (typo, that's mira) this is used directly in Retrofit @Body.
dan: OkHttp behavior: if a request failed during a redirect/401 that triggers Authenticator/Interceptor work, it may attempt to retry the call. For non-repeatable RequestBody, retries will cause duplicate semantics. Historically some platforms buffered the body automatically, but not for streaming. Android 14 emulator networking and the newer okhttp/conscrypt combo made this more visible.
li: log snippet:
```
[12:04:00.123] POST /upload  -> connection reset
[12:04:00.230] Authenticator -> refreshing token on same client
[12:04:00.430] POST /upload  -> body bytes: 1024
[12:04:00.520] POST /upload  -> body bytes: 1024  <-- duplicate
```
li: seems like the client retried after token refresh and also some in-flight call was replayed.
mira: I tried two workarounds locally: 1) disable retryOnConnectionFailure for the client used to send streaming bodies; 2) buffer the body into a temp file / ByteString and use a repeatable RequestBody.
dan: which felt better?
mira: buffering to temp file is reliable but uses disk and increases latency/memory. disabling retryOnConnectionFailure works for connection-related duplicates, but you lose a bit of resilience for flaky networks. Another hybrid is to use a dedicated auth client (like we did for the authenticator issue) and also ensure the uploader client has retry disabled.
li: example fix (buffer to file):
```kotlin
class BufferedBody(private val bytes: ByteArray): RequestBody() {
  override fun contentType() = "application/octet-stream".toMediaType()
  override fun contentLength() = bytes.size.toLong()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) { sink.write(bytes) }
}
// usage: read stream -> ByteArray (or temp file) -> BufferedBody
```
li: or if you want streaming + safety, implement idempotency on the server side (idempotency-key header) and accept duplicates harmlessly.
mira: filed a small sample in the repro repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kotlin-sdk-repros/pull/58 — includes a test that runs on emulator API 34 and toggles retryOnConnectionFailure.
qa-bot: CI run 1287 for branch fix-streaming-upload: https://ci.redwood.dev/build/1287 :eyes:
dan: docs suggestion: add a short note in devex about "Non-repeatable RequestBody + OkHttp retries -> duplicate side effects" and recommended patterns: buffer, disable retry, idempotency headers, dedicated auth client. Also include code snippet for disabling retries per-client.
li: small snippet to disable retries:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(false)
  .build()
```
mira: adding that to onboarding docs. Also will add a sample that demonstrates server-side idempotency header example.
dan: thanks for catching this. Good to include in SDK parity checklist for Android sample apps.
